title: Duran Duran’s Classic Albums Will Be Turned Into Postage Stamps

body: Duran Duran is getting the Royal stamp of approval. Britain’s Royal Mail will issue a range of Duran Duran stamps and collectibles, all of it celebrating the new wave legends’ music. The artwork from eight classic Duran Duran albums will be pressed as official stamps, including the band’s debut self-titled album from 1981, Rio, Seven And The Ragged Tiger, Notorious , the self-titled 1993 comeback collection (known as The Wedding Album ) and 2021’s Future Past . “Celebrating one of Britain’s most innovative and influential bands, this new collection features iconic album artwork, exclusive collectibles and limited-edition memorabilia spanning more than four decades of creativity,” reads a statement from Royal Mail. The headline for the collection reads, “BOLD. VISIONARY. body: TL;DR Getting the most out of Sony headphones and earbuds means relying on the company’s phone app to adjust audio settings. Being able to control devices through apps on our phones is a bit of a double-edged sword. Sure, apps can open up tons of new features, and being able to configure devices remotely lets manufactures simplify hardware designs. But the flip side there is that making even basic changes means that we need our phone — and that’s not always handy. title: Apple Watch can now rewind your conversations, and that’s kinda creepy
summary: Smart glasses, meet your creepy new competition.
body: TL;DR Apple’s new Live Rewind feature can show a text snippet of what was said during the previous 15 seconds. A double-press of the Digital Crown activates it, while Siri can answer questions about the captured text or save it for later. Apple has added visible and audible privacy safeguards, but a watch that can recall what was just said may still feel unsettling. Wouldn’t it be a little creepy if I told you the watch on your wrist could rewind the last 15 seconds of your life? Well, that’s essentially what Apple’s new Live Rewind feature can do. Apple announced the feature alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 today, and despite the slightly creepy premise, it’s easy to imagine situations where it could be genuinely useful. Maybe someone rattled off a Wi-Fi password too quickly, you missed an important number during a conversation, or a colleague said something in a meeting, and you only realized five seconds later that you should probably have been paying attention.
